# Model Check

A **track** is one sequential line of work — a single athlete's journey through the workout, or the shared warm-up, or the shared cooldown; steps in the same track never overlap because they are chained with `afterStep` or other triggers that enforce sequence. A **step** has exactly one duration kind: `fixed` (a number of seconds), `variable` (a range with a default), or `indefinite` (runs until manually stopped). A **startTrigger** anchors a step to the clock (`programStart`, `programStartOffset`) or to another step (`afterStep`, `afterStepWithBuffer`, `manual`, `onAbort`), or to a logical combination of triggers (`compound`). **stepId**s are unique across the WHOLE program, so even if two tracks both have a "rest" step, they must have different stepIds. Every `task` a step occupies — whether "rower", "kettlebell", "box", "sled", or "floor" — needs a matching `resourceConstraints` entry that declares `maxConcurrent`, and the runner enforces that constraint so only as many steps as allowed can use that task at once. Work repeated n times (three athletes doing four rounds at one station each, for example) is declared as `replicates: {count: n, mode: "serial" | "parallel" | "stagger"}` on ONE step — never copied steps or tracks — and you chain what follows each repetition with `instances: "each"`, give the step that waits for all of them `instances: "all"`, and when a holding area between them only fits k at a time, set `replicates.maxInFlight: k` to hold the upstream step back instead of stranding the downstream one.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "tracks are sequential lines of work; one duration kind per step; triggers link steps; every task needs a resourceConstraint; stepIds are global",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "rower", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "kettlebell", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "box", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "sled", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "floor", "maxConcurrent": 3 }
  ],
  "actors": 3
}
```
